newsitem.title: USA: Dole visits Florida, promises to save Medicare.
newsitem.headline: Dole visits Florida, promises to save Medicare.

text.p: Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole began a last-ditch march through the South on Wednesday, trying to catch up to President Bill Clinton in a region Republicans once assumed was firmly in their column.

At a boisterous rally near the waterfront in Jacksonville, Florida, Dole told supporters he wanted to go down in history "as the president who saved Medicare," an emotional issue in this key state, which has a large elderly population.
Behind the scenes, Dole's campaign sent its chairman to Dallas to meet Texas billionaire Ross Perot and ask him to drop out of the race, ABC News reported on Wednesday.
The report said the Dole campaign was asking the Reform Party candidate to end his bid, which has attracted little enthusiasm according to polls, and endorse Dole in his effort to oust Clinton.
Reform Party officials in Dallas said they were not aware of any meeting between Perot and Dole envoys, and flatly rejected suggestions that Perot might withdraw from the race.
"There is absolutely no truth to that. He is in the race to the bitter end. No question," Perot's spokeswoman, Sharon Holmanm, said. "Furthermore, we expect to win."

In Jacksonville, Dole attacked Democrats for spending millions of dollars on advertisments accusing the Republicans of trying to force deep cuts in health insurance programmes for the elderly. Clinton vetoed the Republican Medicare plan, but proposed smaller spending trims of his own.

"There will be no gaps in Medicare and no senior is going to be forced off Medicare in our (budget) plan," Dole said. "He's (Clinton) been so busy playing politics with Medicare that he doesn't have time to fix it. And I will fix it."
Recent polls show Dole and Clinton running neck and neck in Florida, a pivotal and in recent years reliably Republican state. No Democrat has won Florida since former President Jimmy Carter in 1976.
Clinton, also campaigning in Florida on Wednesday, has invested plenty of time and money in the quest for this state's 25 electoral college votes.

Dole stepped up his character attacks on Clinton in Jacksonville, saying: "When I'm elected I will not sell access to the White House, I won't charge you to sleep in the Lincoln bedroom" -- references to recent Democratic fund-raising scandals.

His campaign also began running a new version of an advertisment that criticises Clinton for saying on MTV that if he had it to do over again, he would inhale. Clinton made a now infamous remark during the 1992 campaign that he tried marijuana once but did not inhale.
With only 13 days left until the election, Dole plans stops in Louisiana, Alabama, Texas, Arizona and California later this week.
A strategist for the campaign claimed Dole was shoring up his base in the South, which has become increasingly Republican, but admitted if Dole lost Florida it would be impossible for him to win.

The campaign also plans a major push in vote-rich California in the campaign's waning days, including a bus tour that will begin this weekend. Dole decided to target his resources on the nation's most populous state after a recent poll showed him gaining slightly on Clinton.
But a new Los Angeles Times poll showed Dole 20 points behind in that state. Nationally he lags Clinton by double digits.

At a rally in Macon, Georgia, earlier on Wednesday -- a state Clinton won in 1992 and where Dole has had trouble -- Dole concentated on conservative themes and his plan for a 15 percent tax cut, warning voters not to be fooled by Clinton's recent move to the political middle.
"We want to carry the South, all the way, solid all the way, maybe not (Clinton's home state of) Arkansas, but everywhere else," Dole said. "He's a liberal, he's a liberal, he's a liberal."
